summary: The prepared base already contains the quantization-aware LoRA merge policy from open upstream PR #35975. A real online-FP8 layer reproduced unsafe legacy static-merge behavior, while current auto mode selected dynamic LoRA, explicit merge failed before mutation, and ordinary/mixed boundaries behaved as intended.

tests.what_was_measured: Existing LoRA pipeline policy and lifecycle regression suite: 8 tests passed.

On gfx950, online FP8 transposed a logical (48,32) weight to (32,48) float8 runtime storage; the legacy direct merge raised, current auto selected dynamic, explicit merge rejected without mutation, dynamic output matched an independent BF16 reference within recorded tolerance, ordinary auto still merged, and a mixed module fell back to dynamic.

gpu_execution.evidence: gpu_evidence.log records execution on AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- with actual online FP8 post-load quantization and FP8 base-layer execution.

remaining_limitations: The exact MiniMax-H3 FL2VA model and Larry Turbo LoRA weights were not available.
Only one assigned AMD gfx950 GPU was available, so the reported NVIDIA SM89 TP2 startup/generation path was not reproduced.
The smaller fixture validates the merge-policy mechanism and GPU numerics, not MiniMax-H3 architecture semantics, distributed behavior, video quality, or performance.

On ROCm the legacy direct merge fails first because float8 addmm is unsupported; the reported CUDA execution instead proceeds to the transposed-shape mismatch. Both demonstrate that direct generic merging into runtime FP8 storage is invalid.
